message:
## Vulnerability Digest

Daily sweep for the Products.txt list, covering credible vulnerability reports and material advisory updates observed from 2026-07-26 05:10 IST through 2026-07-27 05:10 IST. No confirmed new product-specific vulnerabilities were verified for the monitored products in this window. A fresh Linux kernel SMB/ksmbd cluster is listed as possible matches needing review because the CVEs are SMB-related and may matter to Ubuntu or SMB server/client deployments, but I did not find a fresh Canonical Ubuntu Security Notice, Samba advisory, or cifs-utils advisory confirming direct product impact in this run.

**Possible matches needing review**

**Linux kernel SMB/ksmbd CVE cluster, published by NVD on 2026-07-25**

- Product: Possible match for Ubuntu and CIFS/SMB-related environments; affected code is Linux kernel SMB server/client paths, not confirmed Samba or cifs-utils.
- Issues: CVE-2026-64388, CVE-2026-64389, CVE-2026-64390, CVE-2026-64391, CVE-2026-64392, CVE-2026-64393, CVE-2026-64394, CVE-2026-64395, CVE-2026-64396, CVE-2026-64397, CVE-2026-64398, CVE-2026-64399, CVE-2026-64400, CVE-2026-64401, and CVE-2026-64437.
- Severity: Not clearly stated by NVD at the time of review; NVD had not provided CVSS enrichment on the sampled records.
- Description: NVD records describe multiple Linux kernel SMB/ksmbd fixes involving permission checks, opener credential handling, path traversal prevention, SMB client behavior, and use-after-free conditions. One example, CVE-2026-64398, reports that an authenticated SMB client could zero file data through FSCTL_SET_ZERO_DATA without an adequate per-handle access check. Another, CVE-2026-64393, concerns SMB2 SET_INFO handlers running path-based VFS helpers with worker credentials instead of opener credentials.
- Why it appears relevant: Products.txt includes Ubuntu and CIFS/SMB Utils. These CVEs are fresh and affect Linux kernel SMB code, which can be present in Linux estates, but the public evidence found during this run did not confirm whether monitored Ubuntu builds or the user-space CIFS/Samba tooling in scope are affected.
- Sources: NVD CVE-2026-64398 https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-64398; NVD CVE-2026-64393 https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-64393; NVD CVE-2026-64437 https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-64437; VulDB recent CVE index https://vuldb.com/cve

**Not included as confirmed findings**

- Broad Linux kernel CVEs newly published by NVD on 2026-07-26 were excluded unless they had a clearer tie to a monitored product or component.
- datamodel-code-generator CVE-2026-63720 was excluded because it is a Python ecosystem package, not the Python runtime listed in Products.txt.
- Microsoft SharePoint CVE-2026-50522 and related SharePoint activity were excluded because they were published or added to KEV before this 24-hour window and SharePoint is not explicitly on the monitored product list.
- MongoDB, Chrome, Firefox, Fortinet, VMware, PostgreSQL, Apache Tomcat, Grafana, 7-Zip, WinRAR, Cisco Nexus/UCS, and other advisories found during the sweep were older than this run's freshness window or appeared only in recap/aggregator coverage.

Closing note: No immediate product-specific action is recommended based on confirmed new findings from this run. A quick owner review is reasonable for systems intentionally using Linux ksmbd/SMB server functionality or Linux SMB client paths, because the possible-match cluster is fresh and SMB-related but not yet confirmed against the monitored product names by a vendor advisory.
